introduction.title: Lists
introduction.explanation: A list keeps many things in order. You can add to the end of it, go through it one thing at a time, or read one item by its index: counted from 0, so item 0 is the first.

realWords.text: A list is called an array. Square brackets make one: [] is an array with nothing in it yet, and boolean[] is the type of an array of booleans.
push adds one item to the end of an array, so the array grows by one. The item to add goes in the round brackets.
for (way of route) is a loop that goes through an array one item at a time. Each time round, way holds the next item, and the loop ends after the last one.
The number in square brackets is an index: an item's place in the array. Indexes count from 0, so route[0] is the first item and route[1] is the second.
length is how many items an array holds right now. The last item's index is always one less than the length, because indexes start at 0.
